title.label: A focus app that keeps distracting you

content.label:
I've been a paying customer of both the Mac and iOS apps, and I use them primarily to help me focus and block out distracting noise while reading and working.

What increasingly bothers me is the "Explore" mode. It's a complete mental overload. Every time I open the app, that's what I'm forced to see, even though all I want is to continue listening to the same three soundscapes that work for me. A focus app shouldn't demand my attention before it helps me focus.
On top of that, even paying subscribers are aggressively pushed toward the lifetime subscription and merchandise. And even in listening mode, one of the most prominent buttons is asking for feedback. I don't want upselling, promotions, or calls for engagement in an app that's supposed to help me focus and wind down.
The core product is great, but the experience around it has become increasingly distracting the exact opposite of what the app is supposed to achieve. A good example of how to ruin a good product.

Ever since becoming a paying subscriber Endel pushes a full-screen app for buying lifetime access in my face every… single… time … I open the app. It is always a „limited time sale“, which somehow still goes on forever and ever. And it’s not even a good price. 

If you looked for a way to annoy your paying customers - congrats, you found it!

Endel itself is great. The sounds are amazing. he iPhone app is good. But the macOS version is just terrible. It was not so great before because it did not offer all soundscapes, but the new version is even worse.

It is an Electron app now, which effectively is a dynamic website and it looks exactly like that. Electron apps also use more memory and CPU resources than necessary and the only reason they exist is to cut development costs. In the age of AI agents being able to create code in no time, there is no excuse to use this lazy technology.

Also, it is not accessible via menu bar anymore (I loved being able to have a mini player there).

The latest update made the desktop app significantly worse. 

The only thing the menu icon is good for now is to quit the app. All other actions there do nothing. At the same time the app window is no longer attached to the menu icon, and you can’t show/hide the app window using the menu icon. Together all this makes the menu icon totally useless. And yet you can’t disable it.

The app doesn’t remember the user preferences between launches: the sound volume is always back to 100%; the last used mode is always set to the first one; the dock icon always set to be visible; the app window is not set to be always on top.

Sadly it looks like the new app was vibe-coded and never really tested before publishing.

I have never regretted having bought this app. It is the best you can do for any kind of situation, any kind of environment, to really focus or get calm.
